articles.title: Rajnath Singh Launches 'Surya': India's First Naval Fleet Support Ship - Jagran Josh
articles.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on October 6 unveiled ‘Surya’, India’s first indigenously developed and built Fleet Support Ship (FSS-1), at Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) in Visakhapatnam. The development marks a massive leap in bolstering the Indian Navy’s logistical potential, operational endurance and naval self-reliance. ‘Surya’ Ship to Act as Naval Logistics Hub Fleet Support Ships are produced to offer critical supplies to maritime vessels while they stay at sea. The 43,500-tonne ‘Surya’ will provide warships and carrier battle groups by offering fuel, fresh water, ammunition, dry provisions and maintenance facilities, thus lowering the need for vessels to return to port. The vessels will also possess improved cargo and fluid capacity, onboard first-line maintenance workshops, a helicopter deck capable of promoting multi-role helicopter missions and self-defence systems. According to the Defence Ministry, such ships are integral for sustaining naval operations over long periods in distant maritime areas. The ‘Surya’ is the maiden of five Fleet Support Ships being developed for the Navy. Singh also laid the keel for FSS-5, marking another milestone in the programme. The five-ship project is estimated at around Rs 19,000 crore. HSL Infrastructure Gets Major Upgrade During the visit, Singh unveiled an advanced Slipway-4 and a 300-tonne Goliath crane at HSL. The upgraded slipway can handle ships of up to 45,000 deadweight tonnes, while the crane is developed to enhance the handling of heavy shipbuilding blocks and promote modern construction methods. Singh stated that the three developments reflected achievement, resolve and evolving shipbuilding potential. He also called for Visakhapatnam to become a massive maritime industrial hub. HAL Koraput Delivers 2,000th Aero-Engine After the Visakhapatnam programme, Singh travelled to Koraput in Odisha, where he saw the delivery of HAL’s 2,000th aero-engine. HAL’s Koraput division has essayed a crucial role in manufacturing and overhauling engines used by India’s military aircraft. The milestone comes alongside initiatives to forge a second production line for Shakti helicopter engines, with an investment of Rs 218 crore. The additional facility is intended to promote indigenous helicopters including the Advanced Light Helicopter Dhruv and Light Combat Helicopter Prachand. Therefore, the two developments underscore India’s extending focus on indigenous shipbuilding, aerospace and defence production as part of its wider ambition for self-reliance in military technology and defence development.

articles.title: Rajnath Singh launches India's first fleet support ship 'Surya' - Manorama Yearbook
articles.content: • Defence Minister Rajnath Singh launched the Fleet Support Ship-1 (FSS-1) ‘INS Surya’ at Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) in Visakhapatnam on October 7. • Designed and built indigenously by HSL, the fleet support ships will feature enhanced cargo and fluid capacity, onboard first-line maintenance workshops, a helicopter deck for Multi-Role Helicopter operations and self-defence systems. • With the fleet support ship programme, the vessels would strengthen the Navy’s reach, endurance and operational effectiveness in the Indian Ocean Region. • A Navy operating for extended periods in distant maritime areas requires not only warships but also logistics, maintenance, sustained support and operational endurance. • Fleet support ships provide this essential capability through at-sea replenishment and sustained support to naval operations. • The launch of FSS-1 Surya is an important step towards strengthening the Navy’s operational reach and endurance. • The minister also laid the keel of the fifth Fleet Support Ship (FSS-5) and inaugurated the upgraded Slipway-4 and 300-tonne Goliath Crane at HSL. • The milestone is a significant step in strengthening HSL’s capacity to build larger and more complex ships and advancing India’s indigenous maritime capability. • As part of enhanced infrastructure to support larger shipbuilding programmes, the upgraded Slipway-4 has been extended and strengthened to enable HSL to build and launch ships of up to 45,000 DWT (deadweight tonnage - the maximum weight a ship can safely carry). • This is a prominent expansion of the shipyard’s capacity to undertake large and complex platforms. • The new infrastructure will strengthen HSL’s ability to undertake larger and more complex shipbuilding programmes and support modern block construction.

articles.title: Bengaluru Police to be Reorganised into Five Commissionerates;Cabinet Approves 1022 New Posts
articles.content: Pramesh S Jain The Karnataka Cabinet has approved a major restructuring of the Bengaluru city police Commissionerate into five separate Commissionerates in the wake of the formation of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA),Home Minister Priyank Kharge said. Under the proposed restructuring,Bengaluru will have East,West,North,South and Central police commissionerates. The existing post of Bengaluru Police Commissioner will be elevated to Chief Commissioner of Police,who will oversee the five Commissionerates. The Cabinet has also approved the creation of 1,022 new police posts to strengthen crime control,traffic management and public safety. The proposed five commissionerates will require a total of around 6,550 posts. Besides the newly sanctioned posts,existing personnel will be redeployed to meet the manpower requirements of the new structure. Six new ACP posts: The traffic wing will also be strengthened.Six new Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) posts will be created,including two for the Central Traffic Division,one each for the West and North Traffic Divisions,and two for the West Law and Order Division. 276 personnel for 11 police stations: The Cabinet has further approved 276 additional personnel for 11 police stations,including stations in the city’s peripheral areas. The establishment of the new police stations and deployment of personnel will be taken up in phases after completion of the recruitment process. The restructuring is aimed at making the police administration more effective in view of Bengaluru’s rapid geographical expansion,rising population and increasing demands on law and order and traffic management,Kharge said.
